series.name: The Sailor & the Showgirl
series.description: Betty Boop has a voice, ambitions, and very definite opinions about how a man should behave. Popeye has a living to earn at sea and a habit of showing his feelings by fixing things. Around the Long Beach waterfront, loving each other means dealing with nightclub work, dangerous employers, long absences, and an old disappearance that still matters. The Sailor & the Showgirl brings romance, screwball comedy, music, and crime into the lives of two familiar characters with plenty left to discover about each other.

series.name: The Jane Chronicles
series.description: Jane Porter chooses a life in Africa. An accident carries her six centuries into the future, to a Baltimore that remembers Tarzan far better than it remembers her. Across three novels, Jane finds work, desire, friendship, and a world whose promises of safety come with difficult conditions. As the past follows her and the country beyond the city opens, she must decide what she wants to build—and who gets a say in the life she calls her own.

series.name: Calder City
series.description: Nancy Drew earns her living asking questions. Blondie Bumstead knows how to make people answer without noticing. Dick Tracy needs evidence he can use. Kent Allard, the Shadow, works by other rules. In Calder City, their investigations cross private bedrooms, expensive hotels, police offices, and the waterfront, where respectable business and criminal power share more than an address. These are adult noir novels about money, appetite, violence, and the price of finding out.

seo.description: Frank Bluto offers Betty Boop twenty-five dollars a night to listen. When she disappears and Mabel is beaten, Popeye comes ashore to find that easy money has become dangerous business.

books.catalogTeaser: Frank Bluto offers Betty Boop twenty-five dollars a night to listen. When she disappears and Mabel is beaten, Popeye comes ashore to find that easy money has become dangerous business.

description.hook: Twenty-five dollars a night. All Betty has to do is listen.
paragraphs: Betty Boop knows how to get men talking. At Frank Bluto’s nightclub, that talent can sell champagne, win a better tip—or earn her money for overhearing conversations the men upstairs would rather keep private.

Betty has plans for herself, and being underestimated has always been useful. But when Popeye comes home with flowers, Betty is missing and her best friend Mabel has been beaten by men asking where she went.

Now a sailor with little patience for explanations has questions nobody wants to answer. Betty has information worth more than her wages. And the people who paid her to listen have very different ideas about what she should do with what she heard.
A waterfront crime adventure with a sharp comic tongue, a dangerous wire reel, and a showgirl determined to have a say in her own rescue.

books.title: My Blue Heaven

description.hook: Betty can hold a room. Holding on to a sailor is another matter.
paragraphs: At the Meridian, the Long Beach nightclub everybody calls Bluto’s, Betty Boop is finding out what her voice can earn her. There are musicians to impress, wages to negotiate, and a stage she wants to make her own.

Popeye has ships to catch. He also has questions about Olive Oyl, who vanished from his life without an explanation. Loving Betty cannot make those questions disappear, any more than loving him can settle what Betty wants from her work.
Songs pass between them. Letters travel too slowly. Homecomings bring pleasures and arguments neither could have managed at a distance.

A prequel to Twenty-Five Dollars a Night, My Blue Heaven returns to the earlier days of their relationship in a musical waterfront romance about desire, ambition, and the practical business of making room for another person without giving up your own life.

paragraphs: That seems an excellent beginning.

With the Meridian still closed after a fire, Betty Boop and Mabel are out of work and thoroughly tired of discussing it. A sailing holiday promises sunshine, good food, and a change of company. Popeye knows his way across the water. Hamish Gravlin—Ham, or “Gravy” when Betty feels like it—has the boat, the manners, and a remarkable ability to avoid ordinary employment.

On the island, Mabel finds someone worth dancing with, Betty finds fresh possibilities for mischief, and the Casino offers more than an evening’s entertainment. Then a photograph gives the search for Olive Oyl an unexpected direction.
A romantic island adventure full of affectionate comedy, theatrical opportunity, and people discovering how much their pleasures—and their loyalties—may cost.

seo.description: Jane Porter chooses Africa. An impossible accident delivers her to Baltimore six centuries later, where Tarzan is remembered and her own future is still hers to invent.

books.catalogTeaser: Jane Porter chooses Africa. An impossible accident delivers her to Baltimore six centuries later, where Tarzan is remembered and her own future is still hers to invent.

description.hook: Jane Porter has decided to stay in Africa. Six centuries have other plans.
paragraphs: In 1913, Jane is ready to build a life she has chosen for herself. She has loved Tarzan and left him. She has work she wants to do, languages to learn, and a father who will have to get used to her decision.
Then a violent anomaly tears her out of that life.

Jane wakes in a Baltimore transformed beyond recognition. Its technology can do things she scarcely knows how to ask for. Its records have already assigned her a place in history. And the people interested in her arrival have reasons of their own for helping her understand it.
There is work here, too. Friendship. The possibility of love. There may even be a way home.
But Jane has learned how easily a woman’s life can become part of somebody else’s plans. The future will have to make room for hers.

paragraphs: Jane Porter has made a place for herself in the twenty-sixth century. She has useful work, people who depend on her, and feelings for Rian Vale that cannot be dismissed because the man she loved in Africa has arrived.

Tarzan has crossed time deliberately. What he finds is a woman whose life has continued without him, in a city that already knows his name. Beyond Baltimore’s managed boundaries lies country he wants to understand—and dangers his old knowledge cannot always answer.
As Jane’s work takes her farther into that country, Tarzan’s example begins attracting attention of its own. People see a promise in him. Some hear only what they want to hear.
An intimate speculative adventure about reunion, competing loyalties, and the difficult discoveries that begin when love survives an impossible distance.

description.hook: The future has people its maps cannot account for. Jane Porter intends to meet them.
paragraphs: Beyond Baltimore’s carefully managed districts, settlements are finding ways to live that the city never planned. Jane’s work brings her into contact with communities whose needs cannot be settled by changing their classification on a screen.

Inside the city, Tarzan’s growing influence is becoming something he never agreed to lead. His name travels farther than his explanations, and people with very different intentions are learning how useful it can be.

Jane has a child to prepare for, two extraordinary men in her life, and responsibilities that reach beyond either relationship. As political pressure grows, the freedom she has fought for must survive decisions with consequences for people far beyond herself.
The concluding volume of The Jane Chronicles carries Jane into a larger, more dangerous world—and asks what it takes to make a future she can live in.

paragraphs: Her client wants photographs of an unfaithful husband. She supplies the time, the place, and directions precise enough to make Nancy wonder why anyone needs a detective at all.

Inside Merriweather’s circle, Blondie Bumstead knows the social arrangements—and how much people reveal to a woman they consider decorative. Elsewhere in Calder City, Dick Tracy and Kent Allard, the Shadow, pursue answers by methods unlikely to satisfy each other.
What begins as a well-paid intrusion into a marriage draws them toward the private dealings of people accustomed to deciding what the city gets to know.
Sex, money, sharp observation, and violence meet in an adult noir novel where recognizing the faces is only the beginning of understanding the company they keep.

paragraphs: The killings barely interrupt Calder City’s business until the victims include a man whose death leaves too much money waiting to be collected. Then the rumors gather around Kent Allard’s other identity.

Dick Tracy has murder files to connect. Nancy Drew has a client who keeps changing hotels and withholding the name of the person she fears. Blondie Bumstead listens for the details a frightened woman has left out.

Richard Wentworth and Nita Van Sloan are doing their own work. As Wentworth’s methods bring the Spider into conflict with the Shadow, the question of who is killing criminals becomes inseparable from what either man believes he is entitled to do.
A noir crime novel of parallel investigations, dangerous certainty, and the people caught between men who believe they can put a city right.
